angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 624,043 km at 69.31 pc = 0.12 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 14.4269 +/- 0.0133 mas (same row, RUWE 1.02): 69.31 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.897 +/- 0.019 solar radii from Hesse et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HD 35843 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..108H/abstract): 624,043 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.94 +/- 0.06 solar masses from Hesse et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HD 35843 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..108H/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5666 +/- 61 K from Hesse et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 35843 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..108H/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Hesse et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 35843 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..108H/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-35843.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.506, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
